;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Mexican Drug War]]
**The [[National Guard (Mexico)|Mexican National Guard]] arrests [[Ovidio Guzmán López]], one of former [[drug cartel|cartel]] leader [[Joaquín "El Chapo" Guzmán]]'s sons, in [[Culiacán]]. He is later released after government forces come under intense attack and are overpowered by [[Sinaloa Cartel]] gunmen, according to Security Minister [[Alfonso Durazo]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-50092641 (BBC News)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/10/18/gun-battles-rock-mexican-city-culiacan-after-el-chapos-son-detained.html (CNBC)]
**According to a later statement, [[President of Mexico|Mexican President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] and government authorities ordered officers to let Guzmán López go free to avoid a "bloodbath" and "preserve the lives of our officers and bring calm back to the city". [https://www.clarin.com/mundo/mexico-panico-tiros-detonaciones-hijo-chapo-guzman-libre_0_qRlCz8Hp.html (''Clarín'')]  
**Eight people are confirmed killed in the failed raid. More than twenty others were injured. [https://apnews.com/e0228a1114fd44f5aff1ace1479ce0f1 (AP News)]
*[[Haska Meyna mosque bombing]]
**Multiple explosions inside a [[mosque]] in [[Haska Meyna District]] of [[Afghanistan]]'s [[Nangarhar Province]] kill at least 62 people and severely damage the building. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-blast/blasts-in-afghanistan-mosque-kill-at-least-62-wound-more-than-100-idUSKBN1WX1AP (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria]]
**The [[Kurds]] say that [[Turkey]] is already violating the ceasefire agreement by shelling the [[Syria-Turkey border|border]] town of [[Ras al-Ayn|Ras al-Ain]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/18/middleeast/syria-turkey-ceasefire-violations-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**Turkish airstrikes kill five [[civilian]]s in the village of Bab al-Kheir. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/deadly-turkish-airstrikes-shatter-deal-to-pause-syria-offensive/ (''Times of Israel'')]

;Arts and culture
*The wreck of [[Japan]]ese warship [[Japanese aircraft carrier Kaga|''Kaga'']], sunk in the [[Battle of Midway]] during [[World War II]], is discovered on the seabed in the [[Pacific Ocean]]. It is only the second vessel sunk during the battle to have been found. [https://www.livescience.com/explorers-find-wwii-warship.html (Live Science)]

;Business and economy	
*[[United Kingdom|UK]] clothing retailer [[Bonmarché]] collapses into administration. The chain employs 2,900 people and operates 318 stores. [https://inews.co.uk/news/business/bonmarche-collapses-into-administration-putting-2900-jobs-at-risk-816818 (iNews)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Seattle crane collapse]]
**[[Washington (state)|Washington State]] authorities find a crane collapse earlier this year in [[Seattle]] was caused when workers removed securing pins too early during the crane's dismantling. Four people were killed in the accident. Three firms are issued fines. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/totally-avoidable-3-firms-fined-deadly-seattle-crane-collapse-n1068466 (NBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Japan]] says it will not join the [[United States|U.S.]]-led [[International Maritime Security Construct]] to protect international shipping in the Persian Gulf and [[Strait of Hormuz]] amid [[Iran]]ian aggression, but will instead deploy its own [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Maritime Self-Defense Force]] to the region to guard merchant vessels "related to Japan". [https://reuters.com/article/uk-mideast-iran-japan/japan-wont-join-u-s-coalition-to-protect-middle-east-shipping-will-send-own-force-idUKKBN1WX0Y4?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Financial Action Task Force]], an international [[counter-terrorism]] finance taskforce, tells [[Pakistan]] to improve its counter-terror funding operations by next February or face being added to the group's blacklist. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/global-anti-terror-body-fatf-gives-pakistan-till-february-to-curb-terror-funding/story-LkMQFwvnhv5OCgszqnOomO.html (''The Hindustan Times'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Trial of Catalan independence leaders]]; [[2019 Catalan protests]]
**[[Catalonia]] goes to a [[general strike]] in protest of the prison sentence of the Catalan independentists leaders. Thousands of demonstrators arrive walking to [[Barcelona]] from the whole region. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/18/catalonia-general-strike-protests-independence (''The Guardian'')] 
**After a peaceful demonstration involving more than 500,000 people in Barcelona, violent clashes erupt, with more clashes in [[Tarragona]] and [[Girona]]. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/videos/politica/disturbios-en-via-laietana/4701189.shtml (''El Periódico'')] [https://tarragonadigital.com/tarragona/carregues-policials-tarragona-manifestacio-18-octubre (''Tarragona Digital'')]
**In Barcelona, a [[water cannon]] is used for the first time against protesters in [[Spain]]. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20191018/471051109292/mossos-tanqueta-agua-disturbios-barcelona-manifestantes.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
*Former [[President of Catalonia]] [[Carles Puigdemont]] is released with charges by the [[Brussels]] prosecutor's office after surrendering on Thursday to the Belgian authorities following the issuing of the [[European Arrest Warrant]] on Monday. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/18/ex-catalan-leader-carles-puigdemont-belgian-authorities-arrest-warrant (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.euronews.com/2019/10/18/former-catalan-leader-carles-puigdemont-walks-free-after-handing-himself-to-brussels-polic (Euronews)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–20 Lebanese protests]]
**Hundreds of protestors march across [[Lebanon]] over [[Lebanese government of January 2019|the government's]] proposal to tax numerous goods, such as [[tobacco]] and [[WhatsApp]] calls. Police respond by firing [[tear gas]] on those in [[Beirut]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/protests-erupt-lebanon-plans-impose-taxes-191017194856354.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lebanon-economy-protests-teargas/lebanon-security-forces-use-tear-gas-in-beirut-protests-idUSKBN1WX01Z?il=0 (Reuters)]
**The government withdraws the controversial tax plan. Despite this, protests continue, with participants swelling to tens of thousands and them now calling for the downfall of the government. [[Prime Minister of Lebanon|Prime Minister]] [[Saad Hariri]] gives his government 72 hours to resolve the country's worsening economic crisis. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/lebanon-protests-economic-crisis-corruption-continue-191018132945814.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 Santiago protests]]
** After a week of fare-dodging protests in the [[Santiago Metro]], thousands of protestors clash with police in different places across [[Santiago]], [[Chile]]. Subway service is suspended in the entire city. Protests started after a price hike in the most expensive subway system in [[Latin America]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/18/chile-students-mass-fare-dodging-expands-into-city-wide-protest (''The Guardian'')]

;Science and technology
*In the [[International Space Station]], the crew members [[Expedition 61]], [[Christina Koch]] and [[Jessica Meir]] took the first [[Women in space|all female]] [[spacewalk]] in history. [https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-50085930 (BBC news)]
